# How to use this book {.unnumbered}

Each chapter follows the same shape, so you always know where to find things.

## The boxes

**This chapter.** A dark strip at the start of each chapter, with the three things it covers.

**Remember.** One line worth keeping, set in italics between two rules. At the end of the chapter, the **Chapter checklist** collects these lines so you can tick them off.

**Build it: Kaveri Kart.** What we add to the running project in this chapter. If you are building along, do this step before moving on.

**Design decision.** A real choice an AI engineer has to make, with the reasoning for each option.

**In production, this goes wrong.** The common ways the chapter's idea fails once real users arrive. These boxes are short, and they are some of the most useful pages in the book.

**Defend your numbers.** Every AI system is full of numbers someone chose: how many test cases, which threshold, how long a text chunk. In an interview or a design review, you will be asked why. This box lists the numbers from the chapter and how to justify each one.

**Practice and Interview corner.** Try them before you turn the page. Answers to both are at the back of the book.

## Code

Code in this book is short and is written in Python. Each listing runs as printed, once you install the package it imports and supply your own data where the text says so. You do not need to type the code to understand the chapter: the text explains what each part does.

## Numbers and prices

Every number about Kaveri Kart is an assumed example, chosen to make the idea easy to see. Prices marked as example prices are made up, to keep the arithmetic simple. Real prices change often, so check your provider's current price page before you plan a budget.
